title: The Unknown Gunshot That Rings in the Dark
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old wiki-summary-derived case file (cases/ep187_...) correctly identified Etsuko Furukawa as the murderer and the ladder/window entry, but it flattened the trick into a vague 'TV timed to a gunshot sound effect' -- the actual mechanism (confirmed by transcript) has no timer device at all: Conan's contact Mr. Tome explicitly confirms no cassette/timer exists in the room. Instead Etsuko exploited her advance knowledge, as the drama's producer, of the precise broadcast second (7:29:32) a gunshot sound effect would air on a show her own company made, and pressed her mother's remote control by hand at that exact instant (enabled by a digital watch she wore only that day), using a dropped handkerchief as cover for bending down. The old file also omits: Katsue was actually killed hours earlier in daylight, not at the moment of the 'gunshot' (the central twist); the living-room TV was deliberately pre-broken by Etsuko that morning so the same sound effect wouldn't play twice; the locked-room element (Katsue's specially-ordered key); Kohji's and Azusa's substantive red-herring motives and alibi details; and the decisive fingerprint clue (Katsue's own prints missing from a remote she used daily, proving it was wiped during an earlier tea-spill cleanup and touched again only by Etsuko). The episode also opens on Katsue having been attacked by an unknown assailant 3 days earlier (the reason Kogoro was hired) -- this thread is never resolved or tied back to Etsuko in the transcript and is left in as an unexplained red herring/backstory hook. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The exact second the 'gunshot' was heard (7:29:32 PM) matches, to the second, the scripted gunshot sound effect in a mystery drama produced by Etsuko's own company -- only its producer could know that broadcast instant in advance.

The remote control recovered from the scene carried only Etsuko's and Azusa's left-hand prints, not Katsue's -- even though Katsue used it daily. Since Azusa had already wiped every object in the room (including the remote) during a tea-spill cleanup earlier that evening, the missing set proves the remote was handled again afterward only by Etsuko.

Kohji reported seeing a blue-white flash light up his mother's window right before the 'gunshot' was heard, then go dark again -- inconsistent with a muzzle flash from a silenced pistol fired hours earlier, but consistent with the bedroom TV switching on and off exactly when the staged gunshot aired.
